item.title: City council & mayor reach budget deal
item.dc:creator: Pat Reporter
item.content:encoded:
The city council and the mayor reached a budget agreement late on Friday after weeks of negotiation over school funding and road repair.

Negotiators from both sides described the talks as tense but productive, noting that the agreement preserves funding for after-school programs while deferring a decision on the new library branch until the spring.

The compromise raises the property tax rate by a small amount and sets aside new money for bridge inspections, officials said.

Residents who attended the public hearing earlier this month said they were relieved a shutdown of city services had been avoided, though several voiced concern about the long-term cost of the pension obligations.

The full council is expected to vote on Tuesday evening at its regular meeting in city hall.
